title: How Your Phone Battery Actually Works

sections.name: Hook
lines: b_hook
Your phone battery is a tiny chemical machine. Every time you charge it, trillions of particles make a journey, and back again.
b_title
Here's what's going on inside, in five steps.

sections.name: Two sides
lines: b_layers
Step one. Inside is a sandwich. On one side, layers of graphite. On the other, a metal oxide packed with lithium. In between, a liquid, and a thin separator.
b_ions
The stars of the show are lithium ions. Tiny charged particles that can swim through that liquid, from one side to the other.

sections.name: Charging
lines: b_charge
Step two. When you plug in, the charger pushes lithium ions across, into the graphite, where they squeeze in between the layers.
b_store
That's stored energy. Like water pumped up a hill, ready to flow back down.

sections.name: Powering your phone
lines: b_discharge
Step three. When you use your phone, the ions flow back. But their electrons can't take the shortcut through the separator.
b_circuit
They have to go the long way, through your phone's circuits. That flow of electrons is the electricity that runs your screen, your camera, everything.
b_gauge
A small chip counts the charge going in and out, and checks the voltage, to estimate your percentage.

sections.name: Why it wears out
lines: b_wear
Step four. With every cycle, a few ions get stuck, trapped in a crusty layer that slowly builds up on the graphite.
b_cycles
Fewer ions means less capacity. Many phones keep about eighty percent after five hundred to a thousand full charges.

sections.name: Making it last
lines: b_heat
Step five. Heat is the biggest enemy. It speeds up the wear, so don't leave your phone in a hot car, or game on it while it charges.
b_range
Batteries are happiest in the middle. Sitting at a hundred percent, or running down to zero, adds extra stress.
b_fast
That's why fast charging races through the first half, then slows down. And why many phones offer to stop at eighty percent.

sections.name: Recap
lines: w_recap
Two sides. Ions in when you charge. Ions back when you use it. Stuck ions wear it out. So keep it cool, and keep it in the middle.
outro
Charge smart, and your battery will last for years. Follow for more of the tech you use every day.
